content.text:
I made two small commits. This crate was already in good shape, so I stopped there rather than churn it. Clippy is clean and all tests pass after each commit.

- **`303de0b`** gives names to the limits that were repeated as bare numbers: 43,200 s, 900 s and 1,209,600 s. They are now `MAX_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_DELAY_SECONDS` and `MAX_RETENTION_SECONDS`, so each value lives in one place. `Tick` keeps its own `MAX_TICK`, because it is a separate limit that only happens to share a value with the retention limit.
- **`17d188d`** moves the "`X` is required" error into one function, `request::missing_parameter`. `Params::require` and `send_message` each built it separately. In `Queue::expire` the closure is now defined after the early return that makes it unnecessary.

I left several things alone on purpose:
- `create_queue` and `set_queue_attributes` have similar but not identical dead-letter and FIFO checks.
- Merging them would risk changing the order in which errors are reported.
- The `.expect("required")` calls after `require` are guarded by the check order SPEC section 2 defines.

I made two small commits. This crate was already in good shape, so I stopped there rather than churn it. Clippy is clean and all tests pass after each commit.

- **`303de0b`** gives names to the limits that were repeated as bare numbers: 43,200 s, 900 s and 1,209,600 s. They are now `MAX_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_DELAY_SECONDS` and `MAX_RETENTION_SECONDS`, so each value lives in one place. `Tick` keeps its own `MAX_TICK`, because it is a separate limit that only happens to share a value with the retention limit.
- **`17d188d`** moves the "`X` is required" error into one function, `request::missing_parameter`. `Params::require` and `send_message` each built it separately. In `Queue::expire` the closure is now defined after the early return that makes it unnecessary.

I left several things alone on purpose:
- `create_queue` and `set_queue_attributes` have similar but not identical dead-letter and FIFO checks.
- Merging them would risk changing the order in which errors are reported.
- The `.expect("required")` calls after `require` are guarded by the check order SPEC section 2 defines.
